item.title: BeOne's FDA Approval in Lymphoma
item.description:
• Summary: BeOne secured FDA approval for its next-generation BCL2 inhibitor in mantle cell lymphoma (MCL), marking the first approval for the company and opening a new therapeutic class beyond Venclexta (venetoclax). The approval was based on robust clinical data showing high response rates. This positions BeOne to compete in the BCL2 inhibitor space and potentially expand into other hematologic malignancies.
  • MoAs: BCL2 inhibitor (induces apoptosis in cancer cells by blocking the anti-apoptotic BCL2 protein)
  • Sources: STAT News, ApexOnco, BioSpace, Endpoints News

item.title: Create Medicines and In Vivo CAR-T
item.description:
• Summary: Create Medicines raised $122 million in Series B funding to advance its in vivo CAR-T platform, which aims to generate CAR-T cells directly inside patients using proprietary vectors. The approach could simplify manufacturing and reduce costs compared to ex vivo CAR-T therapies. The company plans to use the funds to push its lead programs into clinical trials for hematologic cancers.
  • MoAs: In vivo generation of CAR-T cells via targeted delivery of CAR-encoding genetic material
  • Sources: BioPharma Dive, Fierce Biotech, STAT News

item.title: AstraZeneca's Imfinzi Bladder Cancer Trial
item.description:
• Summary: AstraZeneca announced a Phase 3 win for Imfinzi (durvalumab) in a bladder cancer trial, adding to its immunotherapy footprint. The positive results position Imfinzi as a competitor to Keytruda and the Padcev combo from Merck/Pfizer. The trial evaluated Imfinzi as a monotherapy and in combination, showing improved outcomes in a difficult-to-treat population.
  • MoAs: Anti-PD-L1 monoclonal antibody (blocks PD-L1 binding to PD-1, reactivating antitumor immunity)
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma, Endpoints News, ApexOnco

item.title: Degron Therapeutics and Molecular Glue
item.description:
• Summary: Degron Therapeutics raised $40 million to extend its Series A funding, supporting development of its molecular glue degrader platform for immunology and oncology indications. The platform induces proximity between target proteins and E3 ubiquitin ligases to trigger degradation, offering a novel therapeutic modality.
  • MoAs: Molecular glue-induced targeted protein degradation (triggers ubiquitination and proteasomal degradation of disease-relevant proteins)
  • Sources: Endpoints News, BioSpace

item.title: Sun Pharma Chemotherapy Recall
item.description:
• Summary: Sun Pharma voluntarily recalled a batch of a chemotherapy drug in the U.S. due to potential glass particle contamination, raising concerns about manufacturing quality.
  • MoAs: N/A
  • Sources: Fierce Pharma

item.title: Imfinzi NHS Approval for Stomach Cancer
item.description:
• Summary: Imfinzi (durvalumab) is set to become the first immunotherapy approved for stomach cancer patients on the NHS, marking a significant advance in gastric cancer treatment.
  • MoAs: PD-L1 inhibitor (immune checkpoint blockade)
  • Sources: Pharmaceutical Technology
